newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks plummet 4.32 pct at close.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks plummet 4.32 pct at close.

text.p: Worries about the baht's record low plunge against the dollar on Wednesday prompted investors to sell stocks across the board and rake in their profits quickly, brokers said.
The selling closed the SET index down 28.50 points to 631.28 on 7.1 billion baht turnover.

"Investors sold stocks across the board, especially in the banking and finance sectors, and took profits following the fall of baht earlier in the day," said Busaba Kunasirin of Chao Phya Finance and Securities.
A senior dealer with a local bank told Reuters on Wednesday afternoon that the central bank had intervened to stop the baht's fall at around the 32.50/32.60 to the dollar.
Brokers said the intervention by the central bank plus a lack of positive news to boost market investment induced investors to sell stocks.
The focus was on banks and finance firms who released very poor first-half earnings results as anticipated by investors.
Brokers said plans by most Thai commercial banks to release their non-performing loan figures through the exchange on Thursday posed a minimal impact on the market on Wednesday.

"Investors knew a few days ago that banks would release non-performing loans soon. I think the major reason for selling today was purely for profit taking, especially on finance stocks whose prices rose sharply in the past two weeks," said Somnuk Chanrasamee of Nava Finance and Securities.
All key sectors declined on Wednesday. The finance sector was first-ranked in terms of value, losing 6.73 percent, followed by the banking sector declining 6.86 percent.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, falling 11 baht to 107. Nava Finance declined 2.75 to 25.25.
Brokers said they expected the market would continue falling on Thursday if the baht remained weak.
